title: Verifier characterization of zero-error polynomial time
statement: A language over binary strings belongs to zero-error expected polynomial time exactly when there are a polynomial-time verifier and natural numbers $a,k$ such that, on every input $x$, the verifier never returns false if $x$ is in the language and never returns true if $x$ is outside it, for every random string of length $a(|x|+1)^k$, and returns no answer with probability at most $1/2$ under a uniformly random string of that length. Here polynomial time for the verifier means that its true and false outputs are each recognized by a language in polynomial time using the specified self-delimiting pairing of input and random string.
hypotheses_covered: The verifier is efficient in the specified polynomial-time model
The no-false-output condition holds on every member and every random string of the prescribed length
The no-true-output condition holds on every nonmember and every random string of the prescribed length
The probability of returning no answer is at most $1/2$ on every input
